principles: Safe by construction: one null-proto whitelist chokepoint at the entry points makes every downstream read inheritance-proof, instead of guarding ~30 reads individually.
Generalize, do not reinvent: mirror the exact own-prop + Object.create(null) projection B-30c3 shipped for codex/gemini.
Honest scope: defense-in-depth + consistency, not a live-vuln fix; preserve all billing semantics (validator rules, four-field accounting, record shapes) byte-for-byte for legitimate data.
Cheap belt where the chokepoint does not reach: convert residual `in` operators (record validator, openai/shared, streaming) to own-property checks.
Leaf discipline + load-bearing tests: the helper is a pure leaf; a prototype-pollution smoke proves no inherited value reaches a persisted record on every path.
drivers: The ledger reads token fields off externally-derived objects (JSON.parse of provider/CLI stdout, options) via prototype-chain access that would resolve an INHERITED value if Object.prototype were ever polluted; the ledger is billing/usage truth so a silent bogus count is high-consequence.
B-30c3 hardened only the provider extractors; the adapters/assemble/dispatch/streaming/record remainder is inconsistent and a latent foot-gun for the next maintainer.
A genuine Codex host-2 review (B-30c3 F-001/F-002) proved the pattern was worth a systematic sweep; the spec inventoried 48 surfaces and recommended the chokepoint.

options.name: single-null-proto-chokepoint-plus-in-operator-belt
pros: Collapses ~30 surfaces to a handful; downstream reads safe by construction.
Generalizes the shipped B-30c3 strategy; consistent + auditable.
Future new reads are safe automatically; one place to lint.
cons: Must enumerate the per-provider whitelist (already known from the adapters).

options.name: per-read-own-property-guards-everywhere
pros: Minimal/local; mirrors B-30c3 literally per site.
cons: ~30+ edit sites; no structural guarantee; easy to forget on the next new read.

options.name: object-freeze-object-prototype-at-process-start
cons: Risks breaking deps that legitimately write prototypes; far outside the ledger boundary — rejected.

rationale: Per the spec recommendation: a single null-prototype whitelist chokepoint applied at extractRawUsage (assemble.ts) and the anthropic extract (dispatch-usage.ts) makes every downstream adapter/streaming read operate on a null-proto, whitelist-only object — generalizing the exact own-prop/null-proto strategy B-30c3 shipped for codex/gemini and collapsing ~30 prototype-chain surfaces into a handful that are safe by construction. The residual `in` operators (record validator, openai/shared adapters, streaming merge) get the cheap own-property belt. Per-read guards lack a structural guarantee; Object.freeze is out of boundary. Billing semantics are untouched for legitimate own-property data.

preMortem.scenario: The chokepoint drops a legitimate own-property token field (whitelist too narrow), changing a real persisted record.
preMortem.trigger: Whitelist omits a provider field (e.g. a nested detail key or a newer field).
preMortem.consequence: A legitimate token count goes missing from a record — a real billing regression.
preMortem.mitigation: Enumerate the whitelist directly from the existing adapters (anthropic/openai/gemini incl. nested cached_tokens); a smoke asserts a normal (un-polluted) record for each provider is byte-identical before/after the chokepoint (legitimate data preserved).

preMortem.scenario: The smoke pollutes Object.prototype but does not restore it, corrupting later tests in the same process.
preMortem.mitigation: Every pollution is inside try/finally that deletes the key in finally; the smoke asserts Object.prototype is clean again at the end.

preMortem.scenario: A pollution assertion is vacuous (passes even without the hardening) because the test path never actually reads the polluted key.
preMortem.trigger: Asserting on a path the chokepoint already bypassed, or a key no adapter reads.
preMortem.consequence: False confidence; the hardening could regress undetected.
preMortem.mitigation: Each assertion targets a real token key the path reads, and is verified load-bearing (must FAIL against pre-hardening code / with the chokepoint removed).

preMortem.scenario: Converting record.ts `in` to own-prop subtly changes validator behavior for legitimate data.
preMortem.trigger: Touching validation rules while converting the `in` mechanism.
preMortem.mitigation: Convert ONLY the `in` mechanism, not the rules; full npm test (which exercises the B-253e validator) stays green; the smoke asserts legitimate records validate identically.
